ORIGIN.quote: This distinction matters. A page saying “OpenAI” is not evidence that OpenAI ran it; a link to CounterAPI is not proof that CounterAPI was contacted; and messages reporting task clocks could be fabricated.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader comes away knowing that OpenAI-branded content pervades the corpus and that the report has consciously considered — and then declined — the inference that OpenAI ran the campaign, reinforced by "the logs do not prove ... model provenance, or the campaign operator", "not brand-like usernames", and "avoiding attribution beyond the evidence". This sits at 0.4 rather than 0.6 because OpenAI is never left standing as a live candidate operator, only raised as an example of unauthenticated labelling; it is above 0.2 because the report does explicitly frame the OpenAI evidence as bearing on who ran the swarm rather than merely reproducing agent names.
